description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy of two Llama4 models, Scout and Maverick, in solving 5-digit multiplication problems, as a function of their initial confidence levels. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is linear and ranges from 0.91 to 0.98, with tick labels at every 0.01 interval. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linear, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at every 0.2 interval. The Scout model is represented by a solid blue line with circle markers, while the Maverick model is depicted by a dashed orange line with square markers. The Scout model's accuracy starts at approximately 0.8 at an initial confidence of 0.91, peaks at around 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.92, and maintains high accuracy levels, slightly above 0.9, across the remaining confidence levels. The Maverick model's accuracy begins at about 0.6 at an initial confidence of 0.91, decreases to around 0.2 at an initial confidence of 0.98, and shows a general downward trend as initial confidence increases.
